{
  "meta": {
    "title": "Why Token Counts Lie",
    "topicClass": "ai-ml",
    "format": "full",
    "targetLengthSec": 88
  },
  "story": {
    "devices": [
      "question_chapters",
      "failure_before_fix",
      "planted_question",
      "versus_split",
      "object_to_data",
      "semantic_zoom",
      "named_traps",
      "spec_card_ending"
    ],
    "hook": {
      "kind": "problem"
    },
    "runningExample": "One support-chat reply from a customer asking about a delayed order is translated and sent to the model.",
    "chapters": [
      {
        "id": "why_subword",
        "title": "Why not words or chars?",
        "question": "Why not split text into whole words or single characters?"
      },
      {
        "id": "build_piece_list",
        "title": "How is the piece list built?",
        "question": "How does the tokenizer build its fixed list of pieces?"
      },
      {
        "id": "split_differences",
        "title": "Why do token counts differ?",
        "question": "Why does the same text split into different token counts?"
      }
    ],
    "beats": [
      {
        "id": "b1",
        "chapterId": "why_subword",
        "intent": "A support-chat engineer budgets one reply by word count, but the true token count lands differently, and the same reply translated needs 3x more tokens.",
        "device": "failure_before_fix",
        "targetSec": 8,
        "factIds": [
          "fact-20",
          "fact-21",
          "fact-22"
        ],
        "hookNumberIds": [
          "num-5",
          "num-6"
        ],
        "layoutMode": "centered_focus",
        "suggestedPatternIds": [],
        "newTerms": [
          "token"
        ]
      },
      {
        "id": "b2",
        "chapterId": "why_subword",
        "intent": "Two rejected splits fail side by side: characters make thousands of steps, and whole words break on unseen names, so subword is the design that sits between.",
        "device": "versus_split",
        "targetSec": 11,
        "factIds": [
          "fact-4",
          "fact-5",
          "num-3"
        ],
        "layoutMode": "versus_split",
        "suggestedPatternIds": [
          "versus_split"
        ],
        "newTerms": [
          "tokenizer"
        ]
      },
      {
        "id": "b3",
        "chapterId": "build_piece_list",
        "intent": "The reply turns into raw bytes, and the fixed piece list starts from the 256 byte values, so any reply can be written and nothing is unknown.",
        "device": "object_to_data",
        "targetSec": 11,
        "factIds": [
          "fact-1",
          "fact-7",
          "fact-13",
          "num-2"
        ],
        "layoutMode": "pipeline",
        "suggestedPatternIds": [],
        "newTerms": []
      },
      {
        "id": "b4",
        "chapterId": "build_piece_list",
        "intent": "The merge loop counts every neighbouring pair across training text, adds the most frequent pair as one new symbol, and repeats until the fixed piece list reaches 32,000 entries.",
        "device": "semantic_zoom",
        "targetSec": 13,
        "factIds": [
          "fact-7",
          "fact-8",
          "num-1"
        ],
        "continuesPrevious": true,
        "suggestedPatternIds": [],
        "newTerms": [
          "merge"
        ]
      },
      {
        "id": "b5",
        "chapterId": "build_piece_list",
        "intent": "Encoding a new reply replays the learned merges in order, so a common word collapses to one token while an unusual word stays in pieces.",
        "device": "semantic_zoom",
        "targetSec": 10,
        "factIds": [
          "fact-9",
          "fact-10"
        ],
        "layoutMode": "centered_focus",
        "suggestedPatternIds": [],
        "newTerms": []
      },
      {
        "id": "b6",
        "chapterId": "split_differences",
        "intent": "The same reply translated into a language rare in training has few merges of its own, so it stays in small pieces and needs about 3 times as many tokens.",
        "device": "versus_split",
        "targetSec": 12,
        "factIds": [
          "fact-22",
          "fact-10",
          "num-6"
        ],
        "layoutMode": "versus_split",
        "suggestedPatternIds": [
          "versus_split"
        ],
        "newTerms": []
      },
      {
        "id": "b7",
        "chapterId": "split_differences",
        "intent": "Case, leading spaces and digits split differently, so the same name can be one or three tokens; only the exact tokenizer count matches the bill.",
        "device": "named_traps",
        "targetSec": 11,
        "factIds": [
          "fact-15",
          "fact-16",
          "fact-19",
          "num-7"
        ],
        "layoutMode": "stacked_list",
        "suggestedPatternIds": [],
        "newTerms": []
      },
      {
        "id": "b8",
        "chapterId": "split_differences",
        "intent": "The spec card sums the design: byte alphabet, frequent-pair merges, replay to encode, exact counts vary by language.",
        "device": "spec_card_ending",
        "targetSec": 12,
        "factIds": [
          "fact-13",
          "fact-25",
          "fact-18"
        ],
        "layoutMode": "grid",
        "suggestedPatternIds": [],
        "newTerms": []
      }
    ],
    "plantedQuestion": {
      "text": "Why does the same reply, translated into another language, need about 3x more tokens?",
      "beatId": "b1",
      "payoffBeatId": "b6"
    },
    "rejectedAlternative": {
      "beatId": "b2",
      "summary": "Single characters make sequences too long; whole words leave unseen words without an id.",
      "chosenBeatId": "b4"
    },
    "ending": {
      "kind": "spec_card_ending",
      "cta": "Share this with someone who still budgets by word count.",
      "specCard": {
        "lines": [
          "Byte alphabet: all 256 byte values",
          "Merge the most frequent byte pairs",
          "Replay merges; counts vary by text"
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
